\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{этот} (étot)}{этот (étot)}]{\ru{этот} (étot) — this (masculine)}

\label{lesson:RU-C82-this}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a park, then the Russian for a taxi.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{этот}}
\textbf{\ru{этот}} (\emph{étot}) — \textquotedblleft{}this (masculine)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{этот}} is the pointing sound \emph{\ru{э}}, \textquotedblleft{}look\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{\ru{тот}}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer); examples date from the 1500s.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\ru{тот}} (\emph{tot}) — \textquotedblleft{}that (masculine)\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{такой} (takóy)}{такой (takóy)}]{\ru{такой} (takóy) — such, like this}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{такой}}
\textbf{\ru{такой}} (\emph{takóy}) — \textquotedblleft{}such, like this\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ru{такой}} is \emph{\ru{так}}, \textquotedblleft{}so, thus\textquotedblright{}, with an adjective ending, Proto-Slavic \emph{*takŭjĭ}; Vasmer compares Lithuanian \emph{tóks}, \textquotedblleft{}such\textquotedblright{}. It is built as \emph{\ru{какой}}, \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{}, is.
\end{cousinweb}
